title: Add tailguard and ordinal resolver to rescue fragmented SSE payloads and preserve fncall ordering
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: We continue to see production incidents where interleaved or truncated SSE fragments lead to partial JSON emissions or reordered tool/function-call events in the OpenAI compatibility layer. Root causes are (1) late-arriving tail bytes that look like delimiters, (2) ambiguous fragment ordinal assignment across concurrent streams, and (3) heuristic resyncs that sometimes drop fncall ordering metadata. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: a lightweight tailguard that holds a soft buffer for trailing bytes and a deterministic ordinal resolver that assigns and reconciles fragment ordinals across patch/replay windows. The changeset aims to reduce partial-JSON emission and guarantee deterministic ordering of function/tool call handoffs across retries and replays. Implementation notes and checklist: - Introduce sse.tailguard: soft-timeout buffer (configurable per-tenant) that delays final flush for up to N ms when trailing delimiter-like bytes are detected. - Add sse.ordinal_resolver: monotonic per-stream ordinal tag plus reconciliation policy for out-of-order fragments during reassembly. - Emit explicit "watermark" events in the openai-compat layer when ordinals are advanced so downstream SDKs can safely order fncalls. - Improve the stream sanitizer to prefer fence-tokens produced by the ordinal resolver over naive delimiter heuristics. - Add unit/e2e tests that simulate split-utf8, delimiter-spill, interleaved fncalls, and replay scenarios. - Docs: add API note for the public streaming contract changes and new per-tenant tailguard config. Checklist: [x] Tests added/updated [x] Benchmarks (micro) for latency impact [x] Migration note in docs [x] Back-compat notes (watermark events are additive) Related work: Linear ENG-3214, ENG-2987. This description is a single continuous string containing motivation, design summary, and checklist.

review_conversation: Jordan Lee: Can you explain the decision to use a soft buffer instead of adding an explicit frame terminator? We risk added p50 latency.

Author (Priya Kaur): Soft buffer is opt-in (per-tenant) and we observed that an explicit terminator would require protocol bump and break many clients. Tailguard keeps latency impact minimal and is tunable; see microbench results in the PR.
Marisol Alvarez: The ordinal reconciliation looks complex — how does it behave across reconnects and replay?

Author: Ordinals are monotonic tokens attached to each fragment. On reconnect we exchange the last-seen ordinal via the preface and the resolver stitches missing ordinals using deterministic fill rules; duplicate fragments are dropped based on ordinal and checksum. Added tests that simulate the exact reconnect sequence.
Hank O'Neill: We should ensure SDKs ignore watermark events if they are not adopting ordering guarantees yet.
Author: Watermarks are additive and carry a version header. SDKs that do not recognize the header will ignore them; added a note to the streaming contract doc and SDK compatibility test.
requested_changes: Jordan Lee requested a configurable max-tail-delay default of 4ms rather than 10ms for critical low-latency tenants
Marisol asked for stronger assertions in e2e for duplicate-ordinal suppression
author_updates: Changed default max-tail-delay to 4ms for low-latency tier; made config overridable by tenant
Added stronger assertions and a randomized e2e matrix to exercise duplicate suppression
release_notes: Fix streaming partial-JSON and fncall ordering issues by adding tailguard buffering and a deterministic fragment ordinal resolver. Backwards-compatible watermark events added to the OpenAI compatibility layer. Configurable tail delay per-tenant to balance latency vs safety.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: feature gated behind tenant config. Default rollout to staging for 72h health check, then progressive enablement to GA. Monitor stream_error_rate, fncall-misorder, and p50 latency. Alert if fncall-misorder > 0.01% or stream_error_rate increases by 50%.
benchmarks_summary: Microbench: enabling tailguard at 4ms increased p50 by 1.2ms on medium load; tailguard at 10ms added ~3.7ms p50. Reassembly success rate improved from 98.1% -> 99.98% on synthetic interleaved stream tests.
notes_on_compat: OpenAI-compat: watermark events are additive and optional. SDKs that wish to rely on deterministic fncall ordering must opt into watermark handling. Existing clients remain functional without changes.
